segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I wrote my first account, Theophilus, about everything that Jesus began both to do and to teach

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: until the day he was taken up, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles he had chosen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: To them he also presented himself alive after his suffering by many convincing proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And while eating with them, he ordered them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for what the Father had promised,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “which you heard about from me;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when they had come together, they began asking him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, is it at this time that you are restoring the kingdom to Israel?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has set by his own authority,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After saying this, he was lifted up while they were watching, and a cloud took him up out of their sight.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And as they were gazing into heaven while he was going, suddenly two men in white clothes were standing beside them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they said,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they returned to Jerusalem from what is called the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, a sabbath day’s journey away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had entered the city, they went up to the upstairs room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas son of James.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All these were devoting themselves with one mind to prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In those days Peter stood up among the brothers and sisters (the crowd gathered there numbered about a hundred and twenty people) and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Brothers, the scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David about Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for he was numbered among us and was allotted his share in this service.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now this man acquired a field with the wages of his wrongdoing, and falling headlong he burst open in the middle, and all his intestines spilled out.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This became known to all who live in Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his homestead become desolate, and let there be no one living in it,’ and, ‘Let another take his position of oversight.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So then, of the men who accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: beginning from John’s baptism until the day he was taken up from us, one of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they put forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also known as Justus, and Matthias.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they prayed and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two you have chosen

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: to take the place in this service and apostleship from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

notes.traditional: after he had given commands through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen
notes.note: In the Greek this phrase stands between "giving instructions to the apostles" and "whom he had chosen" and could modify either. Most translations, as here, attach it to the giving of instructions. A minority of interpreters read "the apostles whom he had chosen through the Holy Spirit."

notes.traditional: being assembled together with them / while staying with them
notes.note: The verb is rare and its meaning here is disputed. It may mean "eat together," "gather together," or be a variant spelling of a verb meaning "stay with." The sense "eat with" is how ancient translations such as the Latin took it, and it fits Luke's emphasis on the risen Jesus eating with his disciples (Luke 24:41–43; Acts 10:41). Certainty is not possible.

Luke regularly describes angels as men in bright or white clothing. The two "men" at the tomb in Luke 24:4 are called angels in 24:23, and the angel of Acts 10:3 is described as "a man in bright clothing" in 10:30. Readers would have understood these figures as heavenly messengers, though Luke does not use the word here.

This is a measure of distance: the farthest one was permitted to walk on the sabbath under Jewish custom. It was about two thousand cubits, roughly a kilometre or a little over half a mile. The phrase does not imply that the events took place on a sabbath.

The word means someone zealous or ardently devoted, and Luke uses it elsewhere of zeal for the Law or for God (Acts 21:20; 22:3). Whether it marks Simon as belonging to a revolutionary movement is disputed, since an organised party called the Zealots is clearly attested only from the Jewish war of AD 66–70. The traditional rendering is kept, but it may mean no more than "the zealous one."

notes.traditional: the brethren / the brothers (KJV, following a different text: the disciples)
notes.note: The plural of the Greek word for "brother" was the ordinary way to refer to a mixed group of community members, and verse 14 has just said that women were part of this gathering. Many recent translations render it "believers" or "brothers and sisters" for this reason. In verse 16 Peter uses a formal address that is explicitly masculine, and it is translated "Brothers." In verse 14 the same word means Jesus's actual siblings.

The Greek word was an everyday term for service or an assigned task carried out on someone's behalf. "Ministry" is the usual rendering, but it now suggests a clerical profession, which the word did not convey in the first century. The same word recurs in verse 25.

notes.phrase: Now this man acquired a field
notes.note: Verses 18–19 are generally read as an aside by the narrator rather than part of Peter's speech. The phrase "in their own language" and the translation of the Aramaic name are addressed to Luke's readers, not to an audience in Jerusalem. Matthew 27:3–10 gives a different account, in which Judas hangs himself and the chief priests buy the field. How the two accounts relate is debated.

The word normally means "face down" or "headfirst," and that is the rendering of most translations. Some scholars have proposed that it here carries a medical sense, "swollen up," which is how some ancient versions and later traditions about Judas understood the verse. The evidence for that sense is thin, so the usual meaning is kept.

The two quotations are from Psalm 69:25 and Psalm 109:8, in the wording of the Greek version. The first is adapted from the plural ("their homestead") to the singular so that it applies to Judas. "Position of oversight" translates the psalm's word for an assigned charge or office, which older versions rendered "bishoprick" and most modern ones render "office."

In Israel's scriptures, casting lots was a recognised way of leaving a decision to God, used for dividing land and assigning priestly duties (compare Proverbs 16:33). The same Greek word lies behind "was allotted his share" in verse 17, so the replacement is chosen by the same means the language of that verse evokes. This is the last time the New Testament reports the practice among Jesus's followers.

candidates.reason: The plural for community members recurs throughout Acts and the letters, and translators split between 'brothers', 'brothers and sisters' and 'believers'; readers will be confused if it varies by chapter.
'Ministry' versus 'service' is a recurring choice across Acts and Paul, and the word group (with διάκονος, διακονέω) needs one policy.
It is rendered variously as 'time', 'season', 'appointed time' or 'opportunity' across the New Testament, and the contrast with χρόνος needs a consistent treatment.
Translations vary among 'unrighteousness', 'wickedness', 'injustice' and 'wrongdoing', and the word's link to the δικαιοσύνη group makes consistency important.
'Kingdom' versus 'reign' or 'rule' is a pervasive decision for 'the kingdom of God' and should be made once for the whole New Testament.
